extracted.intended_audience: readers of literary criticism, short-story writers, editors, and general readers interested in assessing short-story collections
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for judging short stories and collections (style, voice, translation quality, economy, emotional power, regionalism, etc.), aimed at critics, editors, and informed readers. Focuses on what makes a short story or collection achieve literary permanence and artistic value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity of local/folk portrayal
rubrics_metrics.description: The lives and deaths, joys and sorrows of Connemara peasants are none the less real because they are the product of observation by one who did not live among them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates how convincingly an author renders regional or folk life even if the author is an outsider; examples: Miss Barlow's portraits of Irish fishermen and farmers are judged authentic and closer to the heart of the people than many English writers' efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absence of condescension / sympathetic insight
rubrics_metrics.description: Works should avoid a spirit of condescension and instead show instinctive sympathy and sympathetic insight into subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrast: Miss Barlow's slight condescension is noted as a weakness compared to writers whose instinctive sympathy 'has saved him from that spirit of condescension.' Favorable examples: Armistead C. Gordon's 'instinctive sympathy' toward his subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry in prose / lyrical quality
rubrics_metrics.description: A narrative may 'convey more poetry' into prose fiction; a strong prose voice can possess a poetic or 'poetry of the mind' quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praise is given when an author brings poetic sensibility into short stories (e.g., Miss Barlow, Gibson, the 'poetry of the mind' in allegories). This can elevate collections beyond mere reportage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imaginative power / 'animistic' magic and world-building
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories that maintain an animistic or magical imaginative world (the 'old familiar magic') and present a 'new imaginative world' are highly valued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Algernon Blackwood's work is praised for adequately maintaining the quality of his best animistic work and for creating imaginative worlds such as in 'The Centaur' and 'Pan's Garden.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Passionate reality / emotional truth
rubrics_metrics.description: Narratives should possess a 'passionate reality' that makes characters and situations live before the reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied across genres: Blackwood's and Curie's stories are commended for passionate reality; this criterion values emotional verisimilitude and convincing human portrayal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity to establish or enhance an author's reputation
rubrics_metrics.description: Collections should contain pieces that 'would have made the reputation of a new writer' or otherwise serve as a strong introduction to an author's imaginative life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to judge whether the material is strong and distinctive enough to be a career-making selection; e.g., 'no story in this volume which would not have made the reputation of a new writer' (Blackwood).

rubrics_metrics.name: Serving enduring aesthetic aims / lasting poignancy
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories that serve the 'altar of beauty' or whose magic gains 'greater poignancy as generations pass' are judged to have lasting artistic value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess works by their likely permanence and continuing emotional/aesthetic impact (Blackwood, other major masters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability of the short story as the author's true medium
rubrics_metrics.description: Some writers are judged to have the short story as their 'true literary medium,' producing purer or truer work in that form than in longer forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Phyllis Bottome's short stories 'give a more complete revelation of her talent' and the short story is suspected to be her true medium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Range of subject and mood within a collection
rubrics_metrics.description: A strong collection shows variety—e.g., ranging from tragedy to social comedy—demonstrating breadth of subject and mood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to evaluate whether the collection presents varied emotional and thematic material (Bottome's stories range from tragedy to social comedy). Anthologies are also praised for wide range (Best Russian Short Stories).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subtlety of irony / controlled implicitness
rubrics_metrics.description: Irony that 'pervades' but remains 'definitely concealed' (insistence never evident) is a mark of skill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Looks for layers of meaning and restraint rather than obvious didacticism; Bottome's subtle irony is given as a positive example.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indigenous humor and vivid dramatic power
rubrics_metrics.description: Narratives should capture 'racy humor' and possess vivid dramatic power that is genuinely indigenous to the setting or people portrayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: William Aspinwall Bradley's Kentucky vignettes and their racy humor and vivid dramatic power, comparable to well-known regional writers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realistic, powerful portrayal of war and its passions
rubrics_metrics.description: War stories are judged by their ability to portray the 'naked ugliness of warfare' and the passions it engenders with brutal power and vividness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparative standard invoked: Alden Brooks' narratives are likened to Stephen Crane's 'The Red Badge of Courage' for their portrayal of war.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patterned prose: finding beauty in ugly things; musical rhythmic speech
rubrics_metrics.description: An author's sense of the 'almost intolerable beauty of ugly things' turned into patterns of gracious beauty and 'musical rhythmic speech' is noteworthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thomas Burke's patterned prose and musical rhythms are cited as a mode of transforming grim subject matter into persuasively beautiful language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of translation / idiomatic rendering
rubrics_metrics.description: Translations should be idiomatic and capture subtle nuances; excellence or shortcoming in idiomatic quality is a key evaluative factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Constance Garnett's translations are praised for idiomatic speech; some renderings are 'not thoroughly idiomatic' yet allow the author's imagination to shine (Kuprin). Translation quality affects reception of foreign collections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depth and range of spiritual/psychological observation
rubrics_metrics.description: Sustained and varied spiritual observation—ranging the gamut of human emotion from tragedy to rich comedy—places an author among the great masters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chekhov and Dostoevsky are cited for reflecting every mood of Russian life with subtle artistry and passionate reality; depth of insight into human soul is heavily weighted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy of speech and selection / descriptive and emotional compression
rubrics_metrics.description: A constant economy of selection and an economy of speech—'descriptive and emotional economy'—are virtues of the short story form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeatedly praised (Showerman, Gibson, Maupassant): effective short stories often reveal new aspects on repeated readings and rely on tight selection and compressed expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization: humanity, humor, and inimitable voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Rich humanity and inimitable humor in characterization (a 'mantle of Mark Twain') indicate excellence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Irvin S. Cobb's characterization and humor are singled out as qualities that make stories enduring and memorable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative unity and essential cohesion (justifying form/length)
rubrics_metrics.description: Even stories as long as a short novel must have an 'essential unity of incident' that justifies calling them short stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arthur Machen's 'The Terror' is defended as a short story despite length because of its unity; evaluate cohesion of plot and focus when length approaches novella.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional tension modulated by presentation tone
rubrics_metrics.description: The writer's matter-of-fact tone can enhance emotional tension and engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Machen's use of a 'quiet matter-of-fact air' heightens reader tension; consider how narrative voice and tone affect suspense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery and multilayeredness on repeated readings
rubrics_metrics.description: Collections that 'disclose new aspects after repeated readings' and give a sense of discovery are particularly valuable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Daniel Corkery's 'A Munster Twilight' is praised for revealing new aspects on repeated reading—look for depth that rewards re-reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regionalism as valuable historical/ethnographic record
rubrics_metrics.description: Well-rendered regional stories serve as records of disappearing life and have documentary as well as literary value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: John Fox Jr.'s vignettes are 'valuable records to a later generation'; regional authenticity and atmospheric values contribute to archival worth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allegorical clarity: story-value over esotericism
rubrics_metrics.description: Allegories should be attractive and persuasive; they need not be esoteric to be valuable—story value should not be sacrificed to symbol obscurity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Henrietta Weaver's allegories introduce Persian philosophy but are commended because they remain accessible and retain story value; assess balance of symbol and narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciple-like influence vs independent voice
rubrics_metrics.description: A writer influenced by a master may still be judged by whether he 'can afford to stand alone' beyond discipleship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Richard Curie's work shows Joseph Conrad's influence yet is judged on its ability to stand independently; evaluate both fidelity to influence and originality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economized finality and chiselled utterance
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'chiselled finality of utterance' and careful economizing of brilliance produce strong, often allegorical or prismatic, short pieces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kuprin's pieces achieve a chiselled finality; look for tight, polished endings and a concentrated use of language.
